title: A/R Collection: ID sorts by number value, and ties go by number
custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • Scenario: One customer on A/R Collection has three invoices due the same day whose numbers have different lengths.
  • You are an Admin user (the "Admin" role) working at {Location-A}, your current location.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • Customer {Customer-A} has overdue invoices on today's date.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST S2-14 Fleet.
  • In {Customer-A}'s group there are three open invoices with the same due date, {Document-A}, {Document-B} and {Document-C}, whose numbers have different digit counts, so that in number order they read {Document-A}, {Document-B}, {Document-C} but in letter-by-letter order {Document-B}, {Document-C}, {Document-A}.
    For example: {Document-A} is S1-99, {Document-B} is S1-100 and {Document-C} is S1-101 (the app assigns the real numbers).
  • Starting screen: A/R Collection (Reports, then "A/R Aging Collection" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu) is open in a desktop browser window 1440 px wide, as opened from the Reports menu, with {Customer-A}'s group expanded.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Click the "ID" header.
  2. Click the "ID" header again.
  3. Click the "Due Date" header.
  4. Click the "Due Date" header again.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: rows inside each customer group sort by ID as numbers, never letter by letter, smallest number first: {Document-A}, {Document-B}, {Document-C}.
  • Step 2: largest number first: {Document-C}, {Document-B}, {Document-A}, still in number order.
  • Step 3: rows inside each customer group sort by Due Date, oldest first; {Document-A}, {Document-B} and {Document-C} tie on Due Date, so they are ordered by number, smallest first: {Document-A}, {Document-B}, {Document-C}.
  • Step 4: the Due Date sort reverses, newest first; the three still tie and keep the same order, smallest number first: {Document-A}, {Document-B}, {Document-C} (reversing a sort reverses the sorted column only).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 9 (23 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 26 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11532 (Story 2, Sort by clicking any column header)

  • S2-R4: “ID and No. sort by number value: S1-99 before S1-100 before S1-101. The first click puts the smallest number first and the second click the largest first. The same number-aware order breaks ties in every sort, always smallest document number first: reversing a sort reverses the sorted column only, so tied rows keep that order in both directions. A date column compares the day only, never the time of day, so two rows on the same date are a tie.”
  • S2-R1, A/R Collection columns: “A/R Collection: Date, Location (when shown), Transaction Type, ID, Due Date, Past Due, Amount, Open Balance.”
  • S2-R2: “The first click gives the useful order for the kind of data: text (names, Location, Transaction Type) A to Z; money columns largest first; dates oldest first; Past Due largest first; ID and No. smallest number first (S2-R4). The second click reverses it. The third click repeats the first; there is no unsorted state.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

References from Design

Design canvas "A/R and A/P Report Sorting" (https://claude.ai/artifact/BRYCdjKwGRSgGPC9xxkgF4), read 22 Oct 2026: page 1 "Opening order and header sorting" (board Main.dc.html). Compare the screen with the pictures below at 100% zoom; the expected results still come from the PRD quotes above, the pictures give the look and the on-screen labels.

Design pictures attached to this case:

  • ar-ap-p1-click-the-total-header.png: figure "Click the Total header" (This build (after)), board "1. Opening order and header sorting"
  • ar-ap-p1-a-p-aging-detail-opens-by-vendor-name.png: figure "A/P Aging Detail opens by vendor name" (This build (after)), board "1. Opening order and header sorting"

The design's own words:

  • "First click gives the useful order: money largest first. Second click reverses, third repeats the first. S2-R1, S2-R2, S2-R3, S2-R7." (caption of "Click the Total header")
  • "Buckets stay in fixed order; rows inside each bucket go by vendor name (was most overdue first). S1-R5, S2-R4, S2-R5." (caption of "A/P Aging Detail opens by vendor name")

Difference from the PRD (DD-06), closed: PRD version 5 said A/R Detail and A/R Collection headings written "Transaction type", "Customer full name", "Due date", "Past due", "Open balance" (S2-R1); the design shows the after pictures read "Transaction Type", "Customer Full Name", "Due Date", "Past Due", "Open Balance"; today's production pictures already read the same, with "Location Full Name". Chris Ward ruled on 23 Oct 2026 (answer 4): Title Case on all six reports, on screen, in the PDF and in the CSV, as the design shows; PRD version 9 adds S2-R4a and writes S2-R1 in Title Case. The design's version is now the requirement and this case follows PRD version 9; D-81 (C715563), held until then, is now a normal design case.
